recorded_from_commit: card/205-structural-toc (RE-RECORDED IN PLACE for this card's Fix 1 -- the owner's 2026-10-14 group-gap decision; first recorded against the implementation commit, branched from main at CARD-204's merge)
recorded_from_commit_note: Recorded against this card's own implementation on the merged tree. CARD-204's recording is superseded, not re-recorded in place: this is a different card's deliberate ink change, which the chain's own rule (see every baseline's 'warning' field) says gets a new file under its own card number. Re-recorded in place once, for Fix 1 of this same card (owner decision 2026-10-14: set the structural list's groups apart with TOC_GROUP_GAP_PT of extra white above each level heading). Same card, same page, same deliberate ink change carried one step further -- so this stays one file under CARD-205's number rather than becoming a fourteenth fixture, which is the same rule that gave it its own number in the first place. Interior page 3 is again the only page that moves (3491813 -> 3504840 bytes, measured by a page-by-page digest comparison against the pre-Fix-1 recording, not reasoned about), and the page count is still thirteen: the gaps are white inside a one-page TOC, so no book gets longer on any trim KDP admits.
read_back_through: tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages — the pages decoded out of the exported interior PDF, not the in-memory bitmaps
why_a_new_baseline: CARD-205 replaces the table of contents' per-puzzle listing with a structural one: one 'How to Solve Nonograms' row, a heading plus a 'Puzzles N-M' range row for each non-empty level, and one 'Solutions' row, each (but the headings) carrying leader dots across to its page number. Interior page 3 is the only page whose ink moves -- measured, not assumed: a page-by-page digest comparison against book_baseline_card204.json finds exactly one difference, page 3. The PAGE COUNT is unchanged at thirteen, because this four-puzzle book's TOC was already one page under CARD-200's per-puzzle rule; a larger book's interior does get shorter (the 150-puzzle corpus falls from 310 pages to 307, four TOC pages down to one), which is what tests/helpers/book_corpus.py's CORPUS_PAGE_COUNT records. Fix 1 (owner decision 2026-10-14) then sets the groups apart: TOC_GROUP_GAP_PT (10 pt, 42 px at 300 dpi) of extra white above each level heading -- the blank line the owner's own sample shows -- drawn as a fixed addition to create_toc_page's own pen position and NOT as blank TocEntry rows, so the eight rows AC-1 counts, structural_toc_entry_count and _toc_entries_per_page's uniform division are all exactly what they were. This recording holds page 3 WITH those gaps.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like with CARD-205's structural table of contents in place. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, and an interior_bytes that no longer matches means the written file changed. If a later card deliberately changes either, it records a NEW baseline in a commit of its own, with its own card number, and says so here.
interior_colorspace_note: What every page of this interior declares (CARD-147's own fact, unaffected by CARD-201). NOT the same as each page entry's 'mode' below, which is 'RGB' and always will be: that field is what tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages normalises every page to before digesting it, regardless of the file's own declared colour space.
font_fingerprint_note: This machine's Arial-or-fallback fingerprint, reproduced before this file was written (tests.helpers.book_corpus.font_fingerprint). A machine with a different fingerprint skips the font_dependent_pages below rather than failing on them.
font_dependent_pages_note: Both guide pages (1, 2), the new TOC page (3, CARD-200: its title and every entry are set through _guide_face, the same Arial-or-fallback path the guide and divider pages already use), the three level dividers (4, 6, 8) and the SOLUTIONS divider (10) are machine-lettered. None of the three packed/full answer pages (11-13) are machine-lettered -- a packed slot's band and caption letter in the packaged DejaVu Sans, and so does every page's own new folio (CARD-200: it reuses _band_font, the same packaged face, exactly as the answer caption does -- G-4's reuse, not a new font path), so the folio never makes an otherwise machine-safe page machine-dependent. CARD-205 changes what page 3 says, not the faces it says it in: the title keeps _guide_face at the same size and every row (label, leader dots and page number alike) is set in the same TOC entry face CARD-200 introduced, so page 3 is machine-lettered exactly as before and this list is unchanged.
interior_bytes_note: The black-and-white interior of this book: 3504840 bytes, where this fixture's own pre-Fix-1 recording held 3491813 and CARD-204's held 3441912. Both steps are interior page 3 alone -- the structural TOC's own JPEG stream, whose leader-dot runs carry more high-frequency ink than CARD-200's four plain caption rows did (+49901 bytes), and then Fix 1's group gaps moving three of its eight rows down the page (+13027).
changed_pages_note: Interior page 3 (the table of contents) is the only page that moves against CARD-204's recording, and the only page that moved again when Fix 1's group gaps were added to this card's own earlier recording. Both are measured by a page-by-page digest comparison, not reasoned about: the other twelve pages are byte-identical in both comparisons, which is the evidence that a card touching create_toc_page and the TOC's own entry count reached no other page kind. tests/test_book_pdf_memory.py's TestBookPdfMemory_NonDrawingPagesAreByteIdentical asserts both halves.
